- id=13: color=p, pixels=65, boundary=[[34, 27], [34, 36], [43, 36], [38, 31]] - this is the purple part of the target
- id=14: color=W, pixels=35, boundary=[[39, 27], [39, 31], [43, 35], [43, 27]] - this is the white part of the target
The source is at columns 39-49, which is to the RIGHT of the target (columns 27-36). This is different from the initial state where the source was at columns 25-39.
Wait, the source has moved to the right! Initially, the source was at columns 25-39. After rotating, the source moved to columns 39-49.
So RIGHT not only rotates the source but also moves it to the right. This explains why the stamp went to the right of the target when I rotated and stamped.
Let me reconsider the game mechanics:
- RIGHT: rotates the source clockwise and moves it to the right
- LEFT: does nothing (or maybe it moves the source to the left)
- UP/DOWN: maybe moves the source up/down
- SPACE: stamps the source onto the target
The source starts at columns 25-39 (above the target). After rotating RIGHT, the source moves to columns 39-49 (to the right of the target).
So the stamp position depends on the source's position. When the source is above the target, the stamp goes to the target. When the source is to the right of the target, the stamp goes to the right of the target.
This explains why the stamp went to the wrong place when I rotated the source.
Now, the question is: how do I stamp the BOTTOM half of the target?
If the source is above the target, the stamp goes to the top half. If the source is to the right of the target, the stamp goes to the right of the target.
What if I need to position the source BELOW the target? Then the stamp would go to the bottom half.
But I don't know how to move the source below the target. RIGHT moves the source to the right, and LEFT doesn't seem to do anything.
Wait, maybe LEFT moves the source to the left. Let me try LEFT and see if it moves the source back to the left.
Actually, looking at the source position, it's at columns 39-49. The target is at columns 27-36. So the source is to the right of the target.
If LEFT moves the source to the left, then pressing LEFT should move the source back to columns 25-39 (above the target).
But earlier, when I pressed LEFT, the source didn't change. Maybe LEFT only works when the source is in a specific orientation.
Let me try pressing LEFT and see if it moves the source to the left.
